subject: mathematics
question_text: If θ is the angle between the vectors i + j and j + k, then find sin θ.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.104 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 158. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed VSAQ on its length and shape. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS. Printed appearances: AP 19. sin θ comes from the CROSS product, not the dot product — |a×b| = |a||b| sin θ. A dot-product route would give cos θ and then need an extra conversion. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the magnitudes and a×b
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both vectors have length √2. Then the cross product, laid out as a determinant with i, j, k on top.
steps.memory_tip: Both vectors have length √2. Then the cross product as a determinant with i, j, k on top.

recall.must_convey: That |a| = |b| = √2, a×b = i − j + k and |a×b| = √3.
accept: both lengths are root two and the cross product is i minus j plus k with magnitude root three
compute the cross product as a determinant then take its magnitude
the cross product comes to i minus j plus k
rendu magnitudes root two, cross product magnitude root three
find the magnitudes and the cross product

steps.why: Each vector has a zero component, so one column of the determinant carries a 0 — write it in rather than shortening the row.
common_mistakes: Writing a as i + j + 0k but forgetting the 0 in the determinant row.
Sign slip on the j term.

steps.label: Use |a×b| = |a||b| sin θ
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Rearrange to sin θ = |a×b| / (|a||b|), then substitute.
steps.memory_tip: Rearrange |a×b| = |a||b| sin θ to sin θ = |a×b|/(|a||b|), then substitute.

accept: sin theta is root three over root two times root two which is root three over two
divide the cross product magnitude by the product of the lengths
sin theta comes to root three by two
sin theta root three by two vasthundi
the answer is root three over two

steps.why: sin θ = √3/2 corresponds to θ = 60°, which is what two edge-vectors of a cube meeting at a vertex actually make.
common_mistakes: Using the dot product and reporting cos θ.

insider_note: sin θ needs the CROSS product, so a dot product is no use here. |a||b| comes to exactly 2, which is what makes the answer the standard √3/2.
